The answer is what we have already cited from al-Nawawi: all its narrators transmitted it with the zay, and al-Bayhaqi and al-Daraqutni explicitly stated that it is with the zay, as has preceded.

(p. 137) Among the hadiths indicating the obligation of zakat on trade goods is what Abu Dawud recorded in his *Sunan* from Samura ibn Jundub al-Fazari (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "Amma ba'd: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to command us to give out charity from what we prepare for sale." Abu Dawud (may Allah have mercy on him) remained silent about this hadith, and it is known from his practice that he does not remain silent except about a hadith suitable for use as evidence in his view. Ibn Hajar said in *al-Talkhis* about this hadith: it was narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Daraqutni, and al-Bazzar, from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Samura, from his father, and in its chain is an unknown narrator (jahala).

The author of this commentary (muqayyiduhu), may Allah pardon him, says: In the chain of this hadith in Abu Dawud is Habib ibn Sulayman ibn Samura ibn Jundub, who is unknown (majhul). In it is also Ja'far ibn Sa'd ibn Samura ibn Jundub, who is not strong. In it is also Sulayman ibn Musa al-Zuhri, Abu Dawud, in whom there is laxity (lin). But it is strengthened by the hadith of Abu Dharr that we have already cited, and it is also strengthened by what is established from Abu 'Amr ibn Himas, that his father Himas said: "I passed by 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), and on my neck were hides (udum) that I was carrying. He said: 'Will you not pay your zakat, O Himas?' He said: 'I have nothing but this, and tanned hides (ahib) in qaraz (a tanning plant).' He said: 'That is wealth, so put it down.' So I put it down before him, and he calculated it, and it was found that zakat was obligatory on it, so he took the zakat from it." Ibn Hajar said in *al-Talkhis* about this report: al-Shafi'i narrated it from Sufyan, from Yahya, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Salama, from Abu 'Amr ibn Himas, that his father said: "I passed by 'Umar ibn al-Khattab," and so on. Ahmad, Ibn Abi Shayba, 'Abd al-Razzaq, and Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it from Yahya ibn Sa'id with the same. al-Daraqutni narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Zayd, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Abu 'Amr ibn Himas, from his father, similarly. al-Shafi'i also narrated it from Sufyan, from Ibn 'Ajlan, from Abu al-Zinad, from Abu 'Amr ibn Himas, from his father. End of quote.

Himas is with a kasra on the ha', a light mim, and ends with an unpointed sin. You have seen the establishment of taking zakat from trade goods from 'Umar, and no opponent among the Companions is known for it. This type is called silent consensus, and it is a proof according to most scholars. It is also supported by what al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn 'Umar: "Abu Nasr 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Umar ibn Qatada informed us from his book, that Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim ibn 'Abada informed us, that Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Bushanji narrated to us, that Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, that Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, that 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: There is no zakat on goods (al-'urud) except what is for trade." End of quote.

He said: This is the view of the majority of the scholars. As for what is reported from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), that he said: "There is no zakat on goods," al-Shafi'i said about it in the *Qadim* (his earlier work): the chain of the hadith from Ibn 'Abbas is weak, so following the hadith of Ibn 'Umar is more correct because it is sound, and caution in zakat is more beloved to me. And Allah knows best. He said: Ibn al-Mundhir has related from 'A'isha and Ibn 'Abbas something like what we have narrated from Ibn 'Umar, and he did not report their opposite from anyone, so it is possible that the meaning of his saying, if it is sound, "there is no zakat on goods," is when it is not intended for trade. End of quote from the *Sunan* of al-Bayhaqi. It is supported by what Malik narrated in the *Muwatta'*, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Zurayq ibn Hayyan, and Zurayq was the governor (ʿala jawaz) of Egypt in the time of al-Walid ibn 'Abd al-Malik, Sulayman, and 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz. He mentioned that 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz wrote to him: "Look at whoever passes by you of the Muslims, and take from what appears of their wealth, from what they circulate in trade, from every forty dinars one dinar. What falls short of that, then in proportion, until it reaches twenty dinars. If it falls short by a third of a dinar, leave it, and do not take anything from it."

As for the verse: it is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, spend of the good things you have earned﴾ [al-Baqara: 267], according to how Mujahid (may Allah have mercy on him) explained it. Al-Bayhaqi said in his *Sunan*, in the chapter "Zakat on trade": Allah, the Exalted, the Mighty, said: ﴿O you who believe, spend of the good things you have earned﴾, the verse, informed us Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz, Abu Bakr ibn al-Hasan al-Qadi, and Abu Sa'id ibn Abi 'Amr, they said: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn 'Affan narrated to us, Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, Warqa' narrated to us, from Abu Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿spend of the good things you have earned﴾, he said: trade; ﴿and of what We have brought forth for you from the earth﴾, he said: the date palm. Al-Bukhari said in his *Sahih*, "Chapter on the charity of earnings and trade," due to His saying: ﴿O you who believe, spend of the good things you have earned﴾, up to His saying: ﴿that Allah is Rich, Praiseworthy﴾. Ibn Hajar said in *al-Fath*: he gave this chapter heading only with the verse and without a hadith.

Perhaps he alluded to what Shu'ba narrated from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, concerning this verse: ﴿O you who believe, spend of the good things you have earned﴾, he said: from lawful trade. Al-Tabari and Ibn Abi Hatim recorded it by the route of Adam from him. al-Tabari recorded it by the route of Hushaym, from Shu'ba, and its wording: ﴿of the good things you have earned﴾, he said: from trade; ﴿and of what We have brought forth for you from the earth﴾, he said: (p. 139) from the fruits.

There is no doubt that what Mujahid mentioned is included in the generality of the verse. Thus what we have mentioned of the routes of the hadith of Abu Dharr and the hadith of Samura ibn Jundub, both traced to the Prophet (ﷺ); and what is established from 'Umar taking zakat on hides from Himas; and what is reported from Abu 'Amr and 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz; and the apparent generality of the noble verse; and what Mujahid explained it by; and the consensus of the general body of scholars except one who deviates from the great majority: all of this suffices as evidence for the obligation of zakat on trade goods. And Allah the Exalted knows best.

* *

The fifth issue: on the zakat of debt, and whether debt removes zakat from the debtor or not.

The scholars differed on this. The position of Malik (may Allah have mercy on him) is that a debt a person is owed by another is treated like trade goods in the distinction between the one who runs a trade (al-mudir) and the hoarder (al-muhtakir), and we have clarified this in the issue before this.

His position (may Allah have mercy on him) is that debt prevents zakat on cash and trade goods if it does not exceed what pays it off by the amount on which zakat is obligatory. He said in his *Muwatta'*: "The matter agreed upon among us is that a man may have a debt, and he has goods sufficient to pay what he owes, and he has in addition cash on which zakat is obligatory; then he pays zakat on the cash in his hand on which zakat is obligatory. But if he has nothing of goods and money except enough to pay his debt, then there is no zakat on him, until he has cash in excess of his debt in the amount on which zakat is obligatory; then he must pay zakat on it."

As for livestock, crops, and fruits, debt does not remove the obligation of zakat on them in his view.

The position of Imam al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) is that if the debt is due from a solvent debtor who acknowledges it, or who denies it while the creditor has proof, then zakat on it is obligatory, whether it is cash or trade goods. This is his new position (qawluhu al-jadid). As for his old position (al-qadim), it is that zakat is not obligatory on debt in any case.

If the debtor is insolvent, or a denier with no proof, or one who procrastinates, or absent, then it is in his view like the usurped (maghsub). There is a disagreement about the obligation of zakat on it, and the sound view is that it is obligatory, but it is not taken from him in fact except after it comes into his hand.

If the debt is deferred (mu'ajjal), then there are two opinions:
One of them, from Abu Ishaq: it is like a debt that is due from a poor man or from a denier. So it falls under the disagreement we mentioned just above.

The second, from Abu 'Ali ibn Abi Hurayra: zakat is not obligatory on it; when he receives it, he starts the year anew from it. The first is more correct. This was said by the author of *al-Muhadhdhab*.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 34 (part 6 of 7):

As for when the debt is livestock, such as forty sheep, or is not binding, such as the debt of a mukatab (a slave contracting to buy his freedom), then zakat (almsgiving) is not obligatory on it by agreement among them. If the one who owes has a debt that consumes all his wealth, or after it there does not remain the full nisab (the minimum threshold for zakat), al-Shafi'i said in al-Qadim (his "Old" opinion): the debt that consumes all wealth, or the debt by which the wealth falls below the nisab, cancels the obligation of zakat, because the ownership of it is not stable, since it may be that the ruler takes it for the right of the creditors. He said in al-Jadid (his "New" opinion): zakat is obligatory and the debt does not cancel it, because the two are different in aspect, since zakat is attached to the specific wealth itself while the debt is attached to the liability (dhimmah). And if the owner is placed under restriction (hajr), then there is much disagreement about it.

The soundest view among the Shafi'is is that it is treated according to the ruling on the zakat of usurped property (maghsub), and we have already mentioned its ruling. The Shafi'is also have a third opinion: that the debt prevents zakat in the hidden wealth, which is gold and silver and trade goods ('urud al-tijarah), and does not prevent it in the apparent wealth, which is crops, fruits, livestock and minerals.

The distinction is that apparent wealth grows by itself, unlike hidden wealth. This is the school of Malik as has already been mentioned. The debt owed to a human being and the debt owed to Allah are, according to them, equal in preventing the obligation of zakat.

The school of Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, is that whoever has a debt owed to a solvent (mali') person who acknowledges it and is not procrastinating, it is not incumbent on him to pay its zakat until he receives it. If he receives it, he pays its zakat for the past years.

Something similar was narrated from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. This was also the view of al-Thawri, Abu Thawr, Abu Hanifah and his companions. 'Uthman, Ibn 'Umar, Jabir, may Allah be pleased with them, Tawus, al-Nakha'i, Jabir ibn Zayd, al-Hasan, Maymun ibn Mihran, al-Zuhri, Qatadah, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, Ishaq, and Abu 'Ubayd said: he must pay its zakat immediately, because he is able to take possession of it.

We have already mentioned that this is the view of Malik and al-Shafi'i. If the debt is owed by a poor debtor (mu'sir), or one who denies it (jahid), or one who procrastinates (mumatil), then there are two narrations:

The first: no zakat is obligatory on it. This is the view of Qatadah, Ishaq, Abu Thawr and the people of Iraq, because it is not within his power to benefit from it.

The second: he pays its zakat when he receives it, for the past years. This is the view of al-Thawri, Abu 'Ubayd, and it is narrated from 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, al-Hasan, al-Layth and al-Awza'i that he pays its zakat when he receives it for one year only. This is the view of Malik.

(p-141) The school of Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, is that the debt prevents zakat in the hidden wealth, which is gold and silver and trade goods, and there is no disagreement from him on this. This is the view of 'Ata', Sulayman ibn Yasar, Maymun ibn Mihran, al-Hasan, al-Nakha'i, al-Layth, al-Thawri, al-Awza'i, Ishaq, Abu Thawr, and the companions of ra'y (opinion). We have already mentioned something similar from Malik, may Allah have mercy on him.

Rabi'ah and Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman said: the debt does not prevent zakat in the hidden wealth. We have already mentioned this from al-Shafi'i in his New opinion.

As for the apparent wealth, which is livestock, fruits and grains, the narration from Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, differs. It is narrated from him that the debt prevents zakat in these too, just like the hidden wealth. And in a narration from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim from him: one begins with the debt and pays it, then looks at what remains with him after the expenses of support, and pays zakat on what remains.

No one whose debt exceeds his wealth is obliged to give charity in camels, cattle, sheep or crops, nor is there zakat. This was said by 'Ata', al-Hasan, Sulayman, Maymun ibn Mihran, al-Nakha'i, al-Thawri, al-Layth and Ishaq.

It is narrated that the debt does not prevent zakat in apparent wealth. This was said by al-Awza'i, and we have mentioned it from al-Shafi'i in his New opinion. It is also the view of Malik.

Once you know the views of the scholars on the zakat of debt, and whether it prevents zakat, then know that their disagreement concerning debt is: whether it is zakat-able before it is received, and whether, if one did not pay its zakat before receiving it, the zakat of one year suffices, or it is necessary to pay its zakat for the past years?

The apparent position on this is that it is from the disagreement over the realization of the cause (tahqiq al-manat): is the capacity to obtain (al-qudrah 'ala al-tahsil) like actual attainment (al-husul bi-l-fi'l), or not? We know of no explicit text (nass) from the Book or the Sunnah, nor any consensus (ijma'), concerning the zakat of debt, nor that debt prevents the obligation of zakat on the debtor if it consumes the wealth or reduces it below the nisab, except for reports transmitted from some of the early generations (salaf).

Among them is what Malik narrated in al-Muwatta' from Ibn Shihab, from al-Sa'ib ibn Yazid, from 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, that he used to say: "This is the month of your zakat. Whoever has a debt, let him pay his debt, until your wealth is collected, and then you pay zakat from it."

Among them also is what Malik narrated in al-Muwatta' too, from Ayyub ibn Abi Tamimah al-Sakhtiyani, from (p-142) 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz: that he wrote concerning wealth that some governors had seized unjustly, ordering that it be returned to its people, and that its zakat be taken for the past years. Then he followed that with a letter that only one zakat should be taken from it, for it had been dimar. End of quote. Dimar, with a kasrah on the dad, means: absent from its owner, who cannot take it and does not know its location.

* *

The sixth issue: on the zakat of minerals (ma'adin) and buried treasure (rikaz).

Know that the scholars unanimously agreed on the obligation to take a lawful due from minerals in general, but disagreement arose among them about some cases of this. A group said: no zakat is obligatory on any minerals except gold and silver specifically. So if one extracts from the mine twenty mithqals of gold, or two hundred dirhams of silver, it is obligatory on him to pay a quarter of a tenth (rub' al-'ushr) of that from the time of extraction, and he does not wait a full year (hawl) for it.

Among those who said this are Malik, al-Shafi'i, and the school of Imam Ahmad is like their school. However, Malik requires zakat on all minerals: gold, silver, mercury, lead, copper, iron, ruby, chrysolite, pearl, carnelian, sabaj (a type of stone), kohl, glass, orpiment (zirnikh), ochre (maghrah), and the like. Likewise the flowing minerals, such as pitch (qar) and petroleum (naft) and the like. Their value is assessed at two hundred dirhams or twenty mithqals, apart from gold and silver. So all minerals are zakat-able according to him, and the obligation on them is a quarter of a tenth.

Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, held that the mine is part of the rikaz, so in it, according to him, there is a fifth (khumus). According to him, the rikaz is gold and silver, and what is malleable like iron, copper and lead, according to the more well-known of the two narrations. According to him, the nisab is not a condition for the mine or the rikaz.

Among those who said that a tenth is obligatory on minerals: 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz. The argument of those who said that zakat is obligatory on all minerals is the generality of Allah's saying: ﴿And from what We have brought forth for you from the earth﴾.

The argument of those who said it is obligatory only on the mines of gold and silver is that the original state is the non-obligation of zakat, so it is not obligatory on other than gold and silver, because of the explicit text concerning these two and not others. They also argued with the hadith: "There is no zakat on a stone." It is a weak hadith. Ibn Hajar said in al-Talkhis: Ibn 'Adi narrated it, from the hadith of 'Umar ibn Abi 'Umar al-Kala'i, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, and al-Bayhaqi narrated it from his route, and 'Uthman al-Waqqasi and Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-'Arzami followed him, both from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, and both of them are abandoned (matrukan). End of quote. 'Umar ibn Abi 'Umar al-Kala'i is weak, from the teachers of Baqiyyah among the unknown narrators, as he said in al-Taqrib.

They argued for the obligation of zakat on minerals with what Malik narrated in al-Muwatta' from Rabi'ah ibn Abi 'Abd al-Rahman, from more than one person, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) granted Bilal ibn al-Harith al-Muzani the mines of al-Qabaliyyah, and they are from the direction of al-Fur'. "Those mines, from them, nothing is taken until today except zakat." Ibn Hajar said in al-Talkhis: Abu Dawud, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi also narrated it connected (mawsulan), without the addition: "and they are from the direction of al-Fur'," etc.

Al-Shafi'i said, after narrating the hadith of Malik: "This is not what the people of hadith establish, nor did they establish it, and there is no narration from the Prophet (ﷺ) except his granting of it as an iqta' (land grant). As for zakat other than the khumus, it is not narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ)."

Al-Bayhaqi said: It is as al-Shafi'i said regarding the narration of Malik. It has been narrated from al-Darawardi, from Rabi'ah, connected, and then he cited it from al-Hakim, and al-Hakim cited it in al-Mustadrak. Likewise Ibn 'Abd al-Barr mentioned it from the narration of al-Darawardi. He said: Abu Sabrah al-Madini narrated it, from Mutarrif, from Malik, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Alqamah, from Ibn 'Abbas. I say: Abu Dawud narrated it from both routes. End of quote.

The compiler of this work (muqayyiduhu), may Allah pardon him, says: Using this addition to the marfu' hadith, which Malik mentioned in al-Muwatta', "nothing is taken from those mines except zakat until today," is a kind of inference by reversed presumption (istidlal bi-l-istishab al-maqlub), and it is a valid proof according to a group of scholars among the Malikis and Shafi'is.

Reversed presumption (al-istishab al-maqlub) is: inferring the continuation of a matter in the past from its continuation in the present, since there is nothing in the first state that would change it into the second.

The author of Jam' al-Jawami' said: As for its being established in the first from its being established in the second, that is reversed. It may be said about it: If what is established today were not established yesterday, it would be not established, so the presumption of yesterday would entail that it is now not established, and that is not so; thus it shows that it is established.

He also said in Nashr al-Bunud: It may be said of reversed presumption, to make the inference by it clear: If what is established today were not established yesterday, it would be not established yesterday, since there is no intermediary between establishment and non-establishment. So the presumption of yesterday, free from its establishment, would entail that it is now not established. But that is not so, because it is assumed established now, so this shows that it was established yesterday too. Some Malikis illustrated this with waqf (endowment): when its purpose is unknown but it is found in a certain state, it is applied to that state, because its being in that state is evidence that it was so at the time of the endowment deed. And al-Muhalla illustrated it: a measure (mikyal) existing now is said to have been in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), by presuming the state in the past. Its application to the issue we are dealing with is that the wording "nothing is taken from those mines except zakat until today" indicates by reversed presumption that they were so in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), since nothing changes them, as we have mentioned.

Mukhtasar Marāqī al-Su'ud also pointed to the issue of this presumption in its "Book of Inference" with his saying (rajaz meter):

"And prefer that the presumption is for the original absence (al-'adam al-asli), from this chapter, after the utmost of research
for a text, and it is not found; and this research is necessarily restricted."

Then he said, and this is the point of evidence (mahall al-shahid):

"And what proves for the past the state of the present, is reversed, and the reverse of the free (of establishment)
Like the continuation of what its purpose is unknown, upon what is now, by that it is known."

As for buried treasure (rikaz): in it there is the khumus without dispute, based on his saying (ﷺ): "And in the rikaz is the khumus." The two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), the authors of the Sunan, and Imam Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, except that they differed about what is meant by rikaz.

The majority, including Malik, al-Shafi'i and Ahmad, held that rikaz is the buried treasure of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic era), and that the term rikaz does not apply to minerals.

They argued with what came in the agreed-upon hadith of Abu Hurayrah, part of which we mentioned a little earlier: the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The mine is jubar (unrequited, no liability), and in the rikaz is the khumus." So he distinguished between the mine and the rikaz by the conjunction, which requires difference.

Abu Hanifah, al-Thawri and others held that a mine (ma'din) is rikaz (buried treasure), and they relied on what al-Bayhaqi narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "In rikaz there is one-fifth. It was said: O Messenger of Allah, what is rikaz? He said: Gold and silver that were created in the earth on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth." The majority rejected this, saying that the hadith is weak. Ibn Hajar said in al-Talkhis: al-Bayhaqi narrated it from the hadith of Abu Yusuf, from Abdullah ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from his father, from his grandfather, from Abu Hurairah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ). It was corroborated by Hibban ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Sa'id, but Abdullah is matruk al-hadith (abandoned in narration), and Hibban is weak.

The core of the hadith is established in the Sahih collections and others without the additional wording mentioned. Al-Shafi'i said in al-Jadid: it is a condition for the obligation of the one-fifth in rikaz that it be gold or silver and nothing else. The majority of scholars disagreed with him. Some scholars said: if extracting the mineral involves hardship, then the due is one-quarter of the tenth; and if there is no hardship in it, then the obligation is one-fifth. This has a basis in reasoning, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 41:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾ [the verse].

There is no hiding the severity this noble verse contains regarding going out to jihad in every circumstance. However, He, may He be exalted, made clear the lifting of this severity by His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the ill, nor upon those who find nothing to spend, when they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger﴾ [the verse] [al-Tawbah: 91], so it abrogates it (nasikhah).

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab [Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book]):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾ [the verse].

This noble verse indicates the obligation of going out for jihad in the way of Allah in every circumstance, and other verses have come that indicate the opposite of that, such as His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the ill, nor upon those who find nothing to spend﴾ [the verse] [al-Tawbah: 19 in the source text], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is not for the believers to go forth all together﴾ [al-Tawbah: 122].

The answer is that the verse ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾ is abrogated (mansukhah) by the verses of excuse mentioned, and this case is one of the examples in which the abrogating text (al-nasikh) is itself abrogated, because His saying ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾ abrogates the verses of turning away from the polytheists, and it is itself abrogated by the verses of excuse, as we mentioned just above. And knowledge is with Allah, may He be exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 60:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and for the freeing of slaves﴾.

Al-Shafi'i and al-Layth said: the intended meaning of "the slaves" (al-riqab) is the mukatabun (those who have contracted with their masters for their freedom in exchange for payment, known as mukatabah).

A similar view is narrated from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, al-Hasan al-Basri, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Nakha'i, al-Zuhri, and Ibn Zayd. What supports this view is His saying, may He be exalted, concerning the mukatabun: ﴿and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾ [al-Nur: 33]. Ibn Abbas said: "al-riqab" is more general than the mukatabun, so there is no harm in freeing a slave (raqabah) from zakat, and this is the position of Malik, Ahmad, and Ishaq.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 61:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who abuse the Messenger of Allah—for them is a painful punishment.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, explicitly states that for whoever harms the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) there is a painful punishment.

He mentioned in "al-Ahzab" (Surah al-Ahzab) that such a person is cursed in this world and the Hereafter, and that for him is a humiliating punishment, in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who abuse Allah and His Messenger—Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 57].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 64:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The hypocrites are wary lest a surah be sent down against them﴾ up to His saying: ﴿what you are wary of﴾.

In this noble verse He declares that the hypocrites are wary lest Allah send down a surah that exposes them and makes clear what their inner hearts conceal of wickedness. Then He stated that He will bring out what they were wary of. He mentioned in another place that He does so, namely His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or do those in whose hearts is a disease think that Allah will not bring out their grudges?﴾ [Muhammad: 29] up to His saying: ﴿And you will surely recognize them by the tone of their speech﴾ [Muhammad: 30]. And He showed the intensity of their fear in another place, namely His saying: ﴿They think every shout is against them﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 4].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 74:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They found nothing to resent except that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them.﴾

In this noble verse He states explicitly that the hypocrites found nothing to resent, i.e., to find fault with and criticize, except that Allah bestowed His favour upon them and enriched them through what He opened to His Prophet ﷺ of goodness and blessing.

The meaning is that there is nothing that could be faulted or resented in any way whatsoever. The verse is

• like His saying: ﴿And they resented them for nothing except that they believed in Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾ [al-Buruj: 8],

• and His saying: ﴿And you resent us for nothing except that we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us﴾ [al-A'raf: 126],

• and His saying: ﴿Who have been expelled from their homes without right, only because they say, "Our Lord is Allah"﴾ [al-Hajj: 40].

A parallel from the speech of the Arabs is the saying of Nabigha Dhubyani (al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani, a pre-Islamic poet), in the tawil metre:

"There is no fault in them, except that their swords are notched from the clashing of battalions."

And the saying of another, in the munsarih metre:

"They resent the Banu Umayyah for nothing except that they strike when they are angry."

And the saying of another, in the wafir metre:

"If there is any fault in me, then I am one whose dog is cowardly and whose young camel is lean."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 81:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if only they would understand.﴾

In this noble verse, He, exalted is He, mentions the intensity of the heat of the Fire of Hell, may Allah protect us and the Muslims from it, and He explains this in other places,

• such as His saying: ﴿A Fire whose fuel is men and stones﴾ [al-Tahrim: 6],

• and His saying: ﴿No! Indeed, it is a blazing Fire, stripping away the scalp﴾ [al-A'raf: 15, 16],

• and His saying: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins﴾ [al-Nisa: 56],

• and His saying: ﴿Scalding water will be poured over their heads, by which whatever is in their bellies and their skins will be melted. And for them are maces of iron﴾ [al-Hajj: 19–21],

• and His saying: ﴿And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten metal, which scalds the faces﴾, the verse [al-Kahf: 29],

• and His saying: ﴿And they will be given boiling water to drink, which cuts their intestines to pieces﴾ [Muhammad: 15],

along with other verses.

Note (tanbih)

The scholars differed regarding the morphological pattern (al-wazn al-sarfi) of "Jahannam." Some scholars of Arabic grammar held that its pattern is "fa'anal," so the doubled nun is an added letter, and the root of the word is J-H-M, from tajahhama, meaning "his face frowned," because it meets them with a frowning, scowling face, and their faces frown and scowl in it because of the pain of the punishment they encounter.

From this is the saying of Muslim ibn al-Walid al-Ansari [Tawil meter]:

"I complained to her of my love, and she smiled, and I had never seen a sun smile before her.
So I said to her, 'Be generous,' and she displayed a frown, to kill me, O how beautiful she is when she frowns."

The Arabs say: jahamahu, meaning he confronted him with a disagreeable, gathered face. From this is the saying of Amr ibn al-Fadfad al-Juhani [Tawil meter]:

"Do not frown at us, Umm Amr, for we are afflicted with the sickness of a gazelle whose hunting tools have not betrayed it."

Some scholars said: Jahannam is a Persian loanword (mu'arrab), its original form being "kahinam," which in their language means "the fire," so the Arabs arabicized it and changed the kaf into a jim.

"The Exalted said: ﴿So if Allah brings you back to a group of them and they ask your permission to go out, then say: "You will never go out with me, nor will you fight an enemy with me. You were content with sitting idle the first time, so sit with those who stay behind."﴾ up to His words: ﴿those who remain behind﴾. In this noble verse, Allah punished those who stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk by declaring that they would not be permitted to go out with His Prophet or to fight alongside him (ﷺ), because the ill consequence of opposition leads to the loss of much good.

Something similar has come in other verses, such as His saying: ﴿Those who were left behind will say, when you set out to take spoils: "Let us follow you."﴾ [al-Fath: 15] up to His words: ﴿Thus has Allah said before﴾, and His saying: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights away, as they did not believe in it the first time﴾ [al-An'am: 110], and other verses. The khalif (those who remain behind, the "khalif") is the one who stays behind from the men in the raid and remains with the women and children. From this is the saying of al-Shanfara:

[al-Tawil]
Nor a khalif who remains among the household, sitting in the shade, going and coming, anointing himself with kohl.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 86:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When a surah is revealed, saying: "Believe in Allah and strive along with His Messenger," the men of wealth among them ask your leave and say, "Let us be with those who sit back."﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, mentions that when He sends down a surah containing the command to believe and to strive alongside His Prophet ﷺ, the wealthy among the hypocrites ask permission to stay behind from striving, despite being able to do so, and they ask the Prophet ﷺ to leave them with those who sit back and stay away from the expedition.

In another place He makes clear that this is not one of the attributes of the believers, but is one of the attributes of the doubters (p-148) who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day. This is in His saying: ﴿Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day do not ask your leave to strive with their wealth and their lives, and Allah is Knowing of the God-conscious.﴾ ﴿It is only those who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day, whose hearts are in doubt, who ask your leave, and in their doubt they waver.﴾ [At-Tawbah: 44, 45]. He also made clear that the path (of blame) is against them for this, and that their hearts are sealed, in His saying: ﴿The path (of blame) is only against those who ask your leave while they are wealthy. They are content to be with the women who stay behind, and Allah has sealed their hearts﴾ up to the end of the verse [At-Tawbah: 93]. In other places He showed the intensity of their dread of going out to fighting, such as His saying: ﴿So when a decisive surah is revealed in which fighting is mentioned, you see those in whose hearts is a disease looking at you with the gaze of one fainting from death﴾ up to the end of the verse [Muhammad: 20], and His saying: ﴿So when fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes rolling like one fainting from death. But when the fear departs, they lash at you with sharp tongues﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 19], and to other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 100:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the Muhajirun (emigrants) and the Ansar (helpers), and those who followed them in excellence—Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, explicitly stated that those who followed the foremost, first ones among the Muhajirun and the Ansar, with excellence, are included with them in Allah's good pleasure, in the promise of abiding forever in the Gardens, and in the great triumph. He also made clear in other places that those who followed the foremost with excellence share with them in the good:

• As in His saying, majestic and exalted is He: ﴿And others among them who have not yet joined them﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 3], and so on;

• And His saying: ﴿And those who came after them say, "Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith"﴾ [al-Hashr: 10], and so on;

• And His saying: ﴿And those who believed afterward and emigrated and fought alongside you—those are of you﴾ [al-Anfal: 75].

It is not hidden that He, exalted is He, stated explicitly in this noble verse that He is pleased with the foremost, first ones among the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and those who followed them with excellence. This is a clear Qur'anic proof that whoever reviles them and harbors hatred toward them is astray, opposing Allah, majestic and exalted is He, since he hates those with whom Allah is pleased. There is no doubt that hatred toward those with whom Allah is pleased is opposition to Him, majestic and exalted is He, and rebellion and transgression.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 101:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites, and among the people of Madinah are those who have become accustomed to hypocrisy. You do not know them; We know them﴾ — the verse.

In this noble verse He declares that among the Bedouins and among the people of Madinah there are hypocrites whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) does not know. Allah, exalted is He, mentioned something similar about Nuh (peace be upon him) in his saying: ﴿He said, "And what is my knowledge of what they used to do?"﴾ — the verse [ash-Shu'ara': 112].

(p-149) He also mentioned its like about Shu'ayb, upon them all be the prayers and peace of Allah, in his saying: ﴿The remainder from Allah is better for you, if you are believers. And I am not a guardian over you﴾. End of quotation.

Allah had informed His Prophet about some of the hypocrites, as has passed in the preceding verses, and he informed his companion Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may Allah be pleased with both of them, about some of that, as is well known.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 114:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And the request for forgiveness by Ibrahim for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him﴾.

Here He did not specify this promise that he had made to him, but He explained it in Surat Maryam, with His words: ﴿He said, "Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord. Indeed, He has ever been gracious to me"﴾.

The Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 9, verse 128:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer; [he is] concerned over you, to the believers [he is] kind and merciful.﴾

This noble verse indicates that the sending of this Messenger, who is from among ourselves, who is characterized by these attributes which denote the utmost perfection and the utmost of his compassion for us, is the greatest of the favours of Allah, exalted is He, and the most abundant of His blessings upon us. He has explained this in other places, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah has certainly conferred favour upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves⦆ [Ali 'Imran: 164]

• And His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for ingratitude and caused their people to settle in the house of destruction?﴾ [Ibrahim: 28]

• And His saying: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾ [al-Anbiya': 107]

and other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 129:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Upon Him I have relied, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, commands His Prophet ﷺ to rely upon Him, majestic and exalted is He.

There is no doubt that he complied with this, for he is the master of those who rely upon Allah, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him. Reliance upon Allah, exalted is He, is the way of his brethren among the Messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them.

As Allah, exalted is He, has made clear in other verses, such as His saying concerning Hud, upon him and upon our Prophet be prayer and peace: ﴿He said, "Indeed, I call Allah to witness, and bear witness, you too, that I am free from what you associate with Him, besides Him. So scheme against me, all of you, then do not give me respite. Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord."﴾ [Hud: 54-56] and His saying, exalted is He, concerning Noah: ﴿And recite to them the news of Noah, when he said to his people, "O my people, if my standing [among you] and my reminding you of the signs of Allah is burdensome to you, then upon Allah I have relied. So resolve upon your affair, and [call together] your partners. Then let not your affair be obscured to you; then carry it out against me and do not give me respite."﴾ and His saying, exalted is He, concerning the entirety of the Messengers: ﴿And why should we not rely upon Allah while He has guided us to our ways? We will surely bear patiently what you have harmed us with.﴾

Among the clearest proofs of the greatness of our Prophet's ﷺ reliance upon Allah is his saying on the day of Hunayn, while he was on a mule in that great position:

"I am the Prophet, there is no lie; I am the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib."
